getToken tests the GITHUB_TOKEN binding with if(t) and returns it on the truthy arm; isAuthenticated then tests the stored token positively (s1, s2, f1:2). The CLI fallback supplies an alternative token without reversing this test.

getToken runs child_process.execSync with gh auth token, trims its stdout, and returns it only when the resulting string is nonempty (s4, f1:2). This is a positive output-presence test feeding the authenticated branch.
validateToken binds the awaited fetch response to t and tests t.status and t.ok before reading its JSON username (s5, f1:2). These are decisions on the fetch result in the same scope.

validateToken returns the response JSON username or null after rejecting unsuccessful responses, and s6 requires that returned username to be truthy (s5, s6, f1:2). No negation reverses the successful-response condition on this path.
The tested username and success status come from the registry fetch response, so server_response fits (s5, s6).

AWSModule binds the awaited STSClient.send(new GetCallerIdentityCommand({})) result to te and tests its UserId, Account and Arn fields (s7, f1:2). The STS constructors resolve through bundled module 21644.

initialize returns true only after the identity response has truthy UserId, Account and Arn fields, otherwise continuing profiles and ultimately returning false (s7, f1:2). isValid forwards that result to the positive short circuit in s8.
The condition reads fields of the awaited STS identity response, making server_response appropriate (s7).
GCPModule constructs GoogleAuth and binds the awaited getProjectId and getClient results to t and r before testing t&&r (s9, f1:2). Bundled module 33835 exports GoogleAuth from module 25469.

The t&&r test positively requires both GoogleAuth results and sets isValidCredentials true; isValid returns this flag to the positive short circuit in s10 (s9, s10, f1:2). Initialization failures leave or set the flag false.

The check establishes availability of a GCP project and credential client, so target_artifact fits the credential context (s9, f1:2). GoogleAuth.getClient obtains cached, configured or application-default credentials.

s6 requires the validated response username and either isLinux or isMac before entering s13; the helpers compare os.platform() with linux and darwin (s11, s12). Thus the expression is c8 && (c3 || c4), with a minimum of two conditions.

The successful validation and platform test enables package enumeration and updatePackage calls (s6, s13). updatePackage rewrites the install script, adds the running bundle and invokes publishing processes (f1:2).
The branch activates package updates for an authenticated maintainer on Linux or macOS, with no analysis-detection check in this guard (s6, s11, s12, s13).

The validated username supplies the maintainer whose packages are enumerated, so data_availability fits the credential-dependent operation (s5, s6, s13). The platform alternatives additionally restrict the shell-based update implementation (f1:2).

isValid forwards initialize, whose success comes from the identity-field conjunction in s7 and is retained in callerIdentity (f1:2). s8 requires that single validity condition to execute s14, so the minimum is one.
The positive isValid short circuit enables getAllSecretValues (s8, s14). That method lists secrets and sends GetSecretValueCommand requests using the validated profile (f1:2).
Successful AWS identity validation activates secret collection, rather than detecting an analysis environment (s7, s8, s14).
The identity check establishes a usable AWS profile before secret retrieval, supporting data_availability (s7, s8, f1:2).

The conjunction of the project ID and auth client sets the single isValidCredentials condition returned by isValid (s9, f1:2). s10 requires this condition to execute s15, giving a minimum of one recorded condition.

A present project ID and auth client activate GCP secret collection, with no analysis-detection test in this guard (s9, s10, s15).
